speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Speaker, Sir, on behalf of the Minister for Foreign Affairs, I beg to move, "That the Bill be now read a Second time." Sir, in 1997, Singapore became a State Party to the Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction (CWC).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The licence system requires all entities involved in such activities to apply to Singapore Customs, which is our National Authority for CWC, for a licence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: In a small and densely populated city-state like Singapore, any use of chemical weapons can lead to catastrophic effects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Allow me to remind Members of what transpired in Japan on 20 March 1995, when thousands of Tokyo residents boarded the subway, unaware of the horrific events that were about to transpire.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: That day, a coordinated sarin gas attack carried out by the cult Aum Shinrikyo killed 13 people and injured thousands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: It was later found that in the years leading to the attack, the cult had transported tonnes of chemical precursors to its laboratory for the manufacture of sarin.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: More recently, events involving the alleged use of chemical weapons have gravely threatened the international norm against the use of chemical weapons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Last year, we witnessed two supposed chemical attacks in the United Kingdom involving a nerve agent that caused deaths and serious injury.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The year before, a nerve agent was reportedly used in our own region to assassinate an individual in Kuala Lumpur International Airport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Should such an incident occur on our own shores, the consequences would be profound.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: It is incumbent upon countries to take measures to ensure the safety and security of their population against the use of chemical weapons on their own soil.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: I believe all Members would agree that Singapore should do its utmost in this regard.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Prior to this Bill, the CWPA already provides for controls on the movement of all scheduled chemicals into and out of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: These chemicals have a range of industrial and chemical purposes but could also be weaponised or used in the manufacture of chemical weapons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: As a matter of national security, it is important to ensure that the movement within our borders of all scheduled chemicals which could be used for illicit ends are subject to the proper controls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This is the main objective of the amendments that are being enacted in the present Bill.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Section 9A requires prior approval to be obtained from the Director-General of Customs here before a person transports a prescribed scheduled chemical exceeding a prescribed quantity within Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This Transport Approval can only be granted to certain licensees under the CWPA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This means that, in addition to a CWC licence obtained by a licensee in relation to the use of certain prescribed chemicals, that licensee must also obtain a Transport Approval to transport the prescribed scheduled chemicals within Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This framework has been benchmarked against existing practices by the National Environment Agency (NEA) and the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), which control the transportation of hazardous substances and petroleum and flammable materials respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Section 9B allows the Director-General to cancel or suspend a Transport Approval if necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: An example is if the CWC licensee is convicted of an offence under the CWPA after a Transport Approval was granted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Second, the current requirement for record keeping under the CWPA is limited to information and records for purposes of the CWC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Clause 8 would now require any person who transports prescribed scheduled chemicals exceeding a prescribed quantity within Singapore to keep records in relation to that transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: I now turn to the proposed amendments which will provide additional powers to the Director-General and national inspectors, which include Customs or Police Officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: These powers will allow them to carry out their new roles relating to the control of the transport of scheduled chemicals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: First, the proposed amendments under clause 9 expand the scope for the Director-General to seek information relevant to the transport of any prescribed scheduled chemical within Singapore in contravention of CWPA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The existing CWPA only allows the Director-General to seek information with regard to a declaration which Singapore is required to give under CWC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Second, the scope of "inspection power" and "compliance purpose" have been expanded to cover the transport of prescribed scheduled chemicals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: New inspection powers have been included, such as the sealing of samples taken in relation to the transport of any prescribed scheduled chemical and requiring the owner to send the sample for analysis and bear the costs and expenses arising from the analysis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Such powers will be useful when a national inspector suspects a contravention of the CWPA and has to ascertain if the chemical transported is a prescribed scheduled chemical exceeding a prescribed quantity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This will help ensure the responsible transport of any scheduled chemical within Singapore in accordance with CWPA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Other existing powers, such as interviewing persons working on premises, have also been broadened to include persons found within a vehicle.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: Third, national inspectors will be empowered to take additional action if they have reason to suspect that a vehicle has been or is being used in contravention of the new section 9A.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: In the event that any item is seized, clause 12 allows the Director-General to determine the premises for its storage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The owner must bear the reasonable costs and expenses arising from the storage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This ensures that safe and secure premises are used to store the seized items, which may contain chemical weapons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: I move on to the final set of amendments which expand the scope of matters for which the Minister may make regulations under the CWPA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The proposed amendments under clause 14 allow the Minister to prescribe the fees for an application for a Transport Approval, or for any purpose under the CWPA.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This gives the Minister flexibility to impose fees if the need arises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The current CWPA only allows the Minister to prescribe fees in relation to a licence application, extension or renewal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: This permits regulations to specify imprisonment as a punishment on conviction of an offence in relation to the transportation of scheduled chemicals, among other things.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: These companies include current CWC licensees and member companies under the Singapore Chemical Industry Council.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman) (for the Minister for Foreign Affairs)
text: The companies also submitted suggestions, most of which were accepted and incorporated into the proposed amendments.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Today, more and more industries are using some of these elements, which have the potential to become weaponised, in the wrong hands.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I have a few clarifications for the Minister.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are these criteria clearly set out and are the employees familiar with these criteria and how often are they renewed and updated?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Is there some kind of accreditation for these employees?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there special signages, logos or emblems used for these purposes as well?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Thirdly, transport of these items can take place in various ways.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It could be from specific locations to another location within Singapore.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: How about the transfer of chemical weapons or related chemicals within the same campus or institution but, probably, from one building to the next or within the same building but to another premises?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What about the regulations and requirements for such transfers?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are these also subjected to some kind of framework?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Fourthly, what are the trainings for these "authorised persons and national inspectors” that are mentioned in the Bill?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: They would probably have to go through some niche area themed training as they will be given the power to even seize the items and weapons that are involved.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I hope to have some clarifications on these issues and hope to support the Bill with the clarifications.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: First, let me say that a chemical attack on our shores could claim lives and have serious and permanent health consequences for those affected.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Therefore, we must adopt a proactive approach by ensuring that proper procedures are in place, so that we are well-prepared to address any future threats or incidents.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: With these amendments to the CWPA, we can better manage the risks involved.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef asked whether there were certain criteria and screening processes for persons joining and working in industries dealing with these chemicals.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As part of the licence conditions, these licensees are obliged to ensure the safe and secure handling of the chemicals.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Note that only drivers with an HTDP are allowed to transport CWC scheduled chemicals exceeding a prescribed quantity.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This and other requirements for transporting such CWC scheduled chemicals will be prescribed in the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef also asked whether there were requirements for the vehicles used to transport these chemicals to be clearly marked and labelled.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: There are existing industry standards on labelling, such as the Singapore Standard for Hazardous Chemicals and Dangerous Goods.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Customs is studying these standards and will include them as part of the Transport Approval requirements, where relevant.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The details of these requirements will be prescribed in the subsidiary legislation.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Prof Fatimah Lateef asked if the transport controls applied to the transfer of toxic chemicals within the same campus or institution.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Therefore, the transport of scheduled chemicals within a company's private premises is not covered.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: However, as CWC licensees, companies have an obligation to ensure the safe and secure handling of chemicals within their own private premises.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: For example, for the storage or handling of higher-risk scheduled chemicals, chemical companies are required to adopt mandatory security measures.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The current amendments seek to empower a national inspector to seize any item from a vehicle that the inspector reasonably believes to be the subject matter of, or connected with the commission of, an offence under the new section 9A.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: In the event that toxic chemicals must be seized for further investigations, the authorised persons and national inspectors may tap on the expertise of SCDF and NEA.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: These agencies have experience in the management of items which similarly require careful handling, such as petroleum and flammable materials and hazardous substances.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This will ensure that seizure is done in a safe and secure manner.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They will strengthen Singapore’s regulatory regime on the CWC-scheduled chemicals and enhance public safety and security.
